name: cloud-me
description: Diego's Cloud Me — the personal-administration half of the constellation. Where Cloud SuperApp is the launcher for everything the cloud runs, Cloud Me is the launcher for everything the PERSON runs: paperwork and money (Buro), what is due (Agenda), the public profile (Me), travel and health (Projects) and study (Studying). It stores almost nothing of its own — cards live in Cloud Wallet, passwords in Cloud Vault, files in Cloud IDE, health records in Health Connect — and is the one screen that indexes all of them.

signing._doc: ONE shared Cloud-constellation signing key for ALL Android apps (Cloud-Comms hub+forks, Cloud-Nav, Cloud-Wallet, Cloud-IDE, Cloud-SuperApp). The SAME key signs every app so cross-app signature-IPC + the in-app fleet updater never hit a signature mismatch. KEY LOCATION (raw credential + sops passwords live ONLY in the vault repo): A0_keys/providers/android/release.jks (OU=Cloud Constellation) + A0_keys/providers/android/signing.secrets.yaml. build.sh::_resolve_signing resolves $VAULT_DIR (default ~/git/cloud-vault) + sops-decrypts the passwords, exporting ANDROID_KEYSTORE_FILE/ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD/ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS/ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD which the gradle signingConfig reads. CI does the same via a vault checkout + the SOPS_AGE_KEY secret. THERE IS NO FALLBACK: if the key is unavailable the build FAILS LOUD.

toolchain._doc: Pinned for reproducibility — all derived in flake.nix. Bump here, rebuild devShell.

_doc_modules: Every libs:* entry is shared BY REFERENCE (`dir`) out of ab_cloud-libs-shared/libs — Cloud Me owns no library source of its own. That is the whole design: the app is an assembly. libs:health draws MyHealth, libs:fin draws the accounting dashboard, libs:cal supplies the events and todos behind Agenda. A fix in any of them lands here on the next build with no copy to keep in step.

ui._doc: Cloud Me's whole navigation is this block: five bottom-nav sections in `order`, everything else reached from the hamburger drawer (bottom_nav:false) or the toolbar gear (toolbar:true). A section's `pages` are its tab strip, and a page may declare `pages` of its own — a second strip below the first, which is what Buro > Fin is. Page CONTENT is not here: each page is a file at data/ui/<section>/<page>.json (a sub-page at .../<page>/<sub>.json), loaded by app/build.gradle into `stack_<page id>` at build time. A section with a `target` and no `pages` (Wallet, Health) hands that target to MainActivity.onTarget instead of showing a page of its own — Wallet launches another app, Health jumps to Projects > Health. The same `page:<section>/<page>` grammar arrives from OUTSIDE the app too: the SuperApp's Dashboard icons launch Cloud Me with a `shortcut_action` extra carrying one of these strings.

ui._doc_myfin_mock: Read by libs:fin (UI_MYFIN_MOCK_B64) to draw Buro → Accounting. Copied from the SuperApp; it is still the beta mock the module was written against, not a live aggregator feed.
ui._doc_external_apps: Resolves an `extapp:<id>` target to a package to launch. Cloud Me links out far more than it stores, so this table is load-bearing: a tile whose id is missing here is skipped rather than crashing, which is also how an app you have not installed simply does not appear.

sections._doc: Buro — the paperwork desk, in the order the user reaches for it: Wallet (what is carried), Docs (what is filed), Fin (what it costs) and Vault (what unlocks it). Wallet is the OFFICIAL SOURCE of the wallet data — real files under data/files/wallet/, browsed as folders; Cloud Wallet reads the same records and draws them as 3D cards. Fin is one tab with three sub-pages rather than three tabs, because Acct (what happened), Budget (what is planned) and Portfolio (what is held) are three views of one question.
sections.label: Buro

sections._doc: Agenda — the only section that reads live data with no other app in front of it. Both tabs come from libs:cal: Agenda from CalEngine.events over the next 30 days, Todo from TodoStore, which is the CalDAV VTODO mirror. The user asked for the agenda and todo of Buro AND of health issues; both already land in the same CalDAV account, so the filter is a category on the item, not a second data source.
sections.label: Agenda

sections._doc: Profile — the app's namesake and its centre slot, in two halves: Professional is the LinkedIn profile, Personal is the Instagram one. Both are generated by data/regen-profile.py from the same files the web pages hydrate from, so neither is prose typed twice. The switcher is the section's ordinary tab strip — two pages is all a switcher is here. The app OPENS here — `default: true` — because Profile is the point of an app called Cloud Me, and Buro was only first because it happens to be order 1. The section id stays `me`.
sections.label: Profile

sections._doc: Projects — what is being worked on, travelled to, or studied. Health leads because it is the project that outlives all the others, and because this is now the ONLY MyHealth surface in the constellation: the SuperApp page was deleted and its dashboard icon deep-links here instead. Health is a container tab like Buro > Fin — Summary, Timeline and Configs are three views of one body, not three separate projects. Studying follows as the standing project and Trips is the one with a date. There was a History tab after them: a travel record that never held a single trip, whose page was one note saying so, and which cost a tab slot in every session to say nothing. A record with no entries is not a record, and the trip data that would fill one lives in Cloud Wallet's bookings; when there is a history to show it will be a page under Trips, not a permanent empty tab beside it. Studying was a bottom-nav section of its own until it became a tab here — study management is a project, and the freed bar slot went to Wallet, which is a different app entirely.
sections.label: Projects

pages._doc: Summary — the project-management overview, first because it is the answer to 'what is going on' and every other tab here is one project inside that answer. It is the page the SuperApp used to draw as Projects ▸ My-PM: the same five panels (Calendar, Tasks, Myfin, Myhealth, Nav tracker), except that in the SuperApp four of the five were hardcoded mock numbers with no source, while every one of them is a LIVE surface of THIS app — Agenda reads CalDAV, Buro ▸ Fin draws the accounting dashboard, Projects ▸ Health reads Health Connect. So the panels open the real thing instead of restating a frozen copy of it, and My-PM in the SuperApp becomes a deep link here (extapp:cloud-me#page:projects/pm) exactly as its MyFin and MyHealth dashboard tiles already do. The id is `pm`, not `summary`: Section.page() in Sections.kt resolves a page id across the tab strip AND every sub-strip in one flat list, so a second `summary` in this section would shadow Health's own Summary sub-page and break that tab. Page ids are unique per section, and test-ui-pages.sh now fails when they are not.
pages.label: Summary

pages._doc: Gym — the training programme, and the one page under Health that is NOT a libs:health surface: Summary, Timeline and Configs read Health Connect, while the plan is a decision rather than a measurement and has no record type. It is an ordinary `cards` stack at data/ui/projects/health/gym.json — one item per movement, both names, sets, repetitions, rest, a form note and its own drawable — so editing the programme is editing that list and never Kotlin. It sits here rather than beside it because a workout plan without the body's numbers next to it is a note, not a project.
pages.label: Gym

sections._doc: Wallet — the only bar item that is not a destination. It has no `pages`; its `target` is handed to MainActivity.onTarget, which launches Cloud Wallet. The deck, its expiry dates and its QR codes live in that app, and the bar slot Studying vacated is worth more as one tap to it than as a second copy of it here.
sections.label: Wallet

sections._doc: Health — no longer a section with pages of its own. The MyHealth surface moved to Projects > Health, so the constellation has exactly ONE Health screen: the SuperApp's copy is gone and its dashboard icon deep-links into that page. What is left here is the Wallet idiom — a `target` and no `pages`, so the drawer entry is a shortcut to the page rather than a second copy of it — plus the metric taxonomy below, which libs:health's build.gradle looks up by SECTION ID (`ui.sections[id=health].metrics`) and which therefore cannot move with the pages.
sections._doc_metrics: Data-driven metric taxonomy — read by SummaryPage / TimelinePage / ConfigsPage to render the per-metric tiles + drill-downs. Each metric maps to one-or-more Health Connect record types via `records` (matched at runtime by class simple-name) + the perm subset via `perm_keys`. Add a metric = one entry here + tile icon. Removing a metric here removes it from all 3 top-level pages.
sections.label: Health

sections._doc: Configs — reached from the gear at the top right rather than the drawer, because it is the one destination you want from wherever you are. ONE page, no tab strip: a settings screen is a list you scroll, which is how every other app in the constellation lays its Configs out. Permissions first, then About with the version, the commit and the self-update control, then the way out to the rest of the constellation.
sections.label: Configs

auto_update._doc_max_installs_per_pass: Most install sessions ONE unattended background pass may open. A background pass cannot show the system install dialog (Android 10+ blocks background activity starts), so each install it starts leaves a tap-to-install notification holding a PackageInstaller session until the user answers it. Unbounded, one pass over the 40-entry fleet opens 40 and the installer hits Android's 50-session cap - 'Too many active sessions for UID'. The remainder is picked up by the next pass. User-initiated 'Update all' is NOT capped: it runs in the foreground where the dialog appears and sessions resolve at once.
